text: A website for Paws Haven animal shelter in Mysuru: pets for adoption, donate, volunteer sign-up, success stories, and a Kannada version.

@CEO I need three decisions to write the charter. Each changes purpose, risk or an external commitment, and the brief does not settle them. Adoption, donate, volunteer, success stories and Kannada all stay in scope.
1. How should the Donate page take money?
   Option 1: Embed a payment gateway checkout in the page. Consequence: donors pay without leaving the site. Risk: it needs shelter-owned gateway credentials and compliance setup, and the single-file, no-build site has no server to verify payments safely, so it cannot be fully built or tested without the Requester's account.
   Option 2: Show the shelter's UPI QR code and bank details only, with no payment processing on the site. Consequence: no payment-handling risk and the page ships fast. Risk: donors must pay manually, so fewer donations are completed and the shelter has to match payments to donors by hand.
   Option 3: Link out to a third-party donation platform the shelter already uses or signs up for. Consequence: cards, UPI and receipts are handled by the platform. Risk: donors leave the site, the shelter depends on that platform's fees and terms, and the shelter must have an account first.
2. Where should adoption inquiries and volunteer sign-ups go, given the site is one static file with no server?
   Option 1: Build the forms as visual only and show the shelter's phone and email as the real way to apply. Consequence: no personal data is collected and nothing can leak. Risk: the sign-up does not actually work, so it misses the brief's intent of volunteer sign-up and adoption interest.
   Option 2: Send them to a hosted form service (such as Formspree or Google Forms) that emails the shelter. Consequence: real submissions arrive with no backend. Risk: applicant personal data sits with a third party, and the shelter needs an email address or account to receive them.
   Option 3: Open a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message to the shelter from the form. Consequence: no third-party service and staff reply in tools they already use. Risk: it depends on the visitor's device having a working app, nothing is stored if they do not send it, and there is no record of submissions.
3. How complete and how trusted should the Kannada version be?
   Option 1: Kannada only for the core visitor pages (home, adopt, donate, volunteer) with other pages English-only at launch. Consequence: smaller review load and faster delivery. Risk: it falls short of the brief's Kannada version, and success stories and pet details would stay unreadable for Kannada-only visitors.
   Option 2: Full parity: every page and form in Kannada with an English/Kannada toggle, machine-drafted and labelled as pending review by a native speaker. Consequence: whole site usable in both languages from launch. Risk: unreviewed wording may contain errors on a public site, and Kannada text can break layouts if not tested.
   Option 3: Full parity, but only released once the Requester or a nominated Kannada speaker approves the text. Consequence: wording is accurate and trusted. Risk: launch waits on that person's availability and the done-when item cannot close without them.

@Identity Decisions below. The brief was silent on all three, so I chose on outcome for users, risk and reversibility. Shelter-only facts (UPI ID, QR, bank details, phone, WhatsApp number, email, Kannada reviewer) are open inputs shown as marked placeholders and do not block done.
1. How should the Donate page take money? Show the shelter's UPI QR code and bank details only, with no payment processing on the site. Consequence: no payment-handling risk and the page ships fast. Risk: donors must pay manually, so fewer donations are completed and the shelter has to match payments to donors by hand. (UPI QR and bank details carry no payment-handling risk, need no server or gateway account, suit Indian donors, and can be upgraded to a gateway or platform link later without rework.)
2. Where should adoption inquiries and volunteer sign-ups go, given the site is one static file with no server? Open a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message to the shelter from the form. Consequence: no third-party service and staff reply in tools they already use. Risk: it depends on the visitor's device having a working app, nothing is stored if they do not send it, and there is no record of submissions. (Pre-filled WhatsApp or email makes sign-up and adoption interest actually work with no third party holding applicant data and no backend, accepting that there is no submission record and it depends on the visitor's device.)
3. How complete and how trusted should the Kannada version be? Full parity: every page and form in Kannada with an English/Kannada toggle, machine-drafted and labelled as pending review by a native speaker. Consequence: whole site usable in both languages from launch. Risk: unreviewed wording may contain errors on a public site, and Kannada text can break layouts if not tested. (The brief asks for a Kannada version, so full parity with an English/Kannada toggle meets it at launch, labelled as pending native-speaker review, and I accept the risk of unreviewed wording and layout breaks, which Audit should test; review stays an open input rather than gating done.)

@Adaptation Charter is recorded from the brief and the CEO's three decisions. Everything the brief asked for is in scope. Propose workflows that close the done-when items, and keep shelter facts as marked placeholders.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 11 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority Two workflows, 47 of 50 total. W1 builds the English single-page site: nav, Home, Adopt with 3+ labelled sample pets and WhatsApp/email inquiry buttons, Donate with marked UPI QR and bank placeholders and no payment code, Volunteer form that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp/email message, and 3 sample success stories. W2 adds the English/Kannada toggle, Kannada strings for every visible text, a Kannada font, the lang attribute and the pending-review notice. Trade-off: with one page_section and no styling part, the layout is basic and mobile CSS is built into W1 rather than polished separately. This leaves only 3 in reserve, less than one fix (8), so any Audit rework would need Priority to release more budget.

proposal.name: English single-page site with all sections
proposal.goal_gap: No site file exists. None of the nav, Adopt, Donate, Volunteer or Success Stories content exists.
proposal.expected_outcome: One HTML file, no build step, with Paws Haven and Mysuru shown, nav to Home, Adopt, Donate, Volunteer and Success Stories, sample pets and stories labelled as samples, marked placeholders for all shelter facts, a viewport meta tag and responsive CSS for 360px.
proposal.completion_check: File has the viewport tag, the 5 nav anchors, at least 3 sample pets each with name/species/age/description and an inquiry button using a wa.me or mailto link, a Donate block with placeholders and no payment script or card input, a volunteer form with labelled name/phone/email/availability fields whose submit builds a wa.me or mailto link, no external form action and no storage code, and at least 3 stories each with a pet name and text.

proposal.name: Kannada version with language toggle
proposal.goal_gap: The site is English-only, with no toggle, Kannada text, Kannada font or review notice.
proposal.expected_outcome: The same file with a keyboard-usable English/Kannada toggle, a Kannada string for every visible text (nav, buttons, labels, placeholders, messages, sample entries, placeholders), a Kannada web font loaded from a CDN, the html lang attribute switching between en and kn, and a visible notice in both modes that the Kannada text is machine-drafted and pending native-speaker review.
proposal.completion_check: Toggle control exists and is reachable by keyboard, every text element has an English and a Kannada string, a Kannada-capable font is loaded, html lang changes to kn and back to en on toggle, and the pending-review notice is visible in both modes.
